original.target_description: Study 1 reports four paired post hoc recognition contrasts; supplied locator does not identify a unique outcome contrast. No object-control condition.

replication.target_description: Study 2 reports four original-setup paired post hoc contrasts and additional counterbalanced contrasts; supplied locator does not identify a unique contrast. No object-control condition.

reported_success.location: Study 2, Results and Discussion; accepted manuscript pp. 13, 18
reported_success.quote: Replicating Bernard et al. (2012), the critical interaction effect of Stimulus Gender and Stimulus Orientation was significant [...] the original results from Bernard et al. (2012) are based on stimulus subsets effects that are highly likely to be symmetry-confounds

notes: Both papers obtained and titles verified. No single statistic selected because post hoc analysis alone is not a unique test locator. Original candidates: upright vs inverted males t(77)=6.29, p<.001; upright vs inverted females t(77)=1.38, p=.17; inverted females vs males t(77)=5.42, p<.001; upright males vs females t(77)=0.54, p=.59. Replication original-setup counterparts: t(59)=5.18, p<.001; t(59)=1.22, p=.23; t(59)=3.91, p<.001; t<1 without exact p. The narrative success verdict applies collectively to original-setup post hoc tests, with the authors' symmetry-confound caveat. Requested test-statistic metric would be t if a contrast were specified. No conversion performed.
